newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says ready to mop up excess liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says ready to mop up excess liquidity.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday the bank was ready to mop up liquidity once the new round of reserve requirement cut takes effect on July 4.
"The (Central Bank), through its open market operations, is prepared to mop up the liquidity arising from the policy change if inflationary pressures set in," Singson said in a statement.
In January, the Central Bank announced a two-tiered reduction in banks' reserve requirements as part of its move to lower intermediation costs.
The first reduction of one percentage point took effect on January 3.
The second reduction of yet another percentage point, which will take the reserve requirement down to 13 percent, will release additional funds of 6.5 billion pesos into the already liquid system.

The Central Bank has been increasing its benchmark overnight and term reverse repo rates in recent days, but traders said banks have not been buying the reverse repos waiting for rates to rise further.
Singson said a part of the excess liquidity could be drained by a new reserve requirement of 13 percent being imposed from July 4 on bank trusts and other fiduciary accounts.

The country's reserve money level was 17.8 billion pesos lower than the programmed level in the first four months of the year, while domestic liquidity, or M3, was 41.1 billion pesos lower during the four-month period.
